session.title: Session 1
session.synopsis: Displaced from a Vegas Greyhound bus into dimensional freefall, four strangers awaken in the Library of the Fates, fending off planar ink beasts before stumbling into the haven of The Margin.

editorialForum.summary: Forensic telemetry, active trade-offs, and historical PR change records.

segments.text: Pierre knelt and gently offered his open hand to the swinging driftwood doll.
"Would you like a ride?"

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 11: THE ROAD TO THE MARIGOLD
blocks.text: The doll stopped swiping at the grass and looked up at Pierre with its coral eyes. "A ride would be grand. Thanks, mate."

segments.text: The doll stopped swiping at the grass and looked up at Pierre with its coral eyes.
"A ride would be grand. Thanks, mate."

blocks.text: Pierre carefully placed the doll on his shoulder, letting its driftwood legs settle against his rucksack strap. As they followed the road down the fence line, Pierre leaned his head slightly toward his tiny passenger.

segments.text: Pierre carefully placed the doll on his shoulder, letting its driftwood legs settle against his rucksack strap. As they followed the road down the fence line, Pierre leaned his head slightly toward his tiny passenger.

blocks.text: "I heard them say a word back there... 'half-blood,'" Pierre murmured in his quiet cadence. "Do you know this word?"

segments.text: "I heard them say a word back there... 'half-blood,'"
Pierre murmured in his quiet cadence.
"Do you know this word?"

blocks.text: "Half-blood? Yeah, I think I've heard of that before," the doll replied thoughtfully, adjusting its needle rapier. "Last time I knew where I was, me mates and me were on a ship, sailing through dark, scary waters like this. And now I'm a puppet."

blocks.text: "They say Mount Olympus moved to America, you know," Pierre mused. "Maybe America is more magical."

blocks.text: Ahead of them, the wooden fence opened toward a clearing in the woods, flanked by the decaying uprights of an old gate.

segments.text: Ahead of them, the wooden fence opened toward a clearing in the woods, flanked by the decaying uprights of an old gate.

blocks.text: Through the broken gate, a crackling campfire illuminated an older, sun-weathered man and a young girl resting near the flames. Carrying the doll securely on his shoulder, Pierre followed Eusacles and Dravin toward the fire.

segments.text: Through the broken gate, a crackling campfire illuminated an older, sun-weathered man and a young girl resting near the flames. Carrying the doll securely on his shoulder, Pierre followed Eusacles and Dravin toward the fire.

blocks.text: "Hello," Pierre called out cautiously. "We are looking for where we are."

segments.text: "Hello,"
Pierre called out cautiously.
"We are looking for where we are."

blocks.text: The man turned from the fire, looking up with an easy smirk and raising a hand in greeting. "Huh? No way. What's up? Welcome to the Margin."

segments.text: The man turned from the fire, looking up with an easy smirk and raising a hand in greeting.

blocks.text: Dravin stepped forward into the warm firelight, his brow furrowing. "What edit killed us?"

blocks.text: Overhead, the decrepit archway formerly read *The Marigold Inn*, but weather and rot had worn away the letters until only *The Margin* remained.

segments.text: Overhead, the decrepit archway formerly read *The Marigold Inn*, but weather and rot had worn away the letters until only *The Margin* remained.

blocks.text: Pierre stared up at the rotting timber, whispering softly, "The Margin..."

blocks.text: Eusacles rolled his shoulders with a dry chuckle. "Welcome to the afterparty, I guess."
